title: Depth-first search (recursive)
summary: Go as deep as possible before backtracking: pre-order, visited, reachability.
hints: `dfs_visit(g, u, visited, order)` has three jobs: mark `u` visited, append `u` to `order`, then for each neighbour `v` of `u` that is not visited, call `dfs_visit` on `v`. The recursion is the stack.

`dfs_order` creates `visited` (all false) and `order` (empty), calls `dfs_visit` once from `start`, and returns `order`. Note that the helper takes both by reference so every call shares the same ones.
`reachable(g, from, to)`: run the same traversal and check whether `to` was visited, e.g. `dfs_visit` from `from`, then return `visited[to]`. (`from` reaches itself.)
